# A legacy system's exercised behaviour is pinned as reviewable avowries before anyone changes it
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #295, sha256:e39884fe94cb505ef2ec38472ab117011aca3a1a858ad066a7ae47bc8d30aafc). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Draft
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (future; characterization capture only, slice 1 of 2)
- **Milestone:** M5 Synthesis (future)
- **Source:** board refinement of a product idea, reviewed by the product manager, an architect and a domain expert (characterization testing). Existing code that a team is afraid to change can be stabilised by characterization specs (golden-master tests) that pin its current observable behaviour before it is edited. Written as avowries, the same specs later become the bridge to other targets (card 296) and a strangler-fig migration path. Related: drift resistance (card 289), which measures the same protection for code written in Avowry.
- **Depends on:** 030 (synthesize Avowry from existing code; this card supplies the behaviour oracle that synthesis is checked against)
- **Story:** As Morgan, I want an inherited C# system's exercised behaviour captured as avowries that pass on the unchanged code, so that I can change it and see at once which pinned behaviour moved.
- **One user-observable outcome:** Morgan runs one command against a legacy fixture and gets avowries that pass unchanged, fail on any planted change to a captured outcome, and a report of what was and was not exercised.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given a legacy fixture with known outcomes, including a planted known bug, When characterization runs, Then it emits Given/When/Then avowries that pass against the unchanged fixture and fail on each planted change to a captured returned, stored, emitted or failed outcome, and the report names every planted change no avowry caught. ZOMBIES: Z no exercised case gives an explicit empty result, never a pass; O one case gives one passing avowry; M distinct cases stay distinct; B boundary inputs are kept; I the runner contract (how outcomes are observed) is explicit; E observed failures are characterized, the planted bug included and tagged as a known quirk; S capture is the same on a rerun.
  2. Given two captures in a row, When volatile values (timestamps, IDs, unordered collections, number formatting) pass through declared scrubbers, Then the two outputs are byte-identical, and any difference with no scrubber fails the capture (never retried until it passes). ZOMBIES: Z no volatile value needs no scrubber; O one scrubbed timestamp; M several scrubbers compose; B a value that is volatile only sometimes; I each scrubber is named in the report; E an unscrubbed difference fails with the field named; S scrubbers do not hide a planted change.
  3. Given a completed capture, When the report is read, Then it shows a coverage measure of the legacy code (for example branch coverage) and names the unexercised paths, and each assertion is marked essential or incidental by a reviewer before it is accepted (incidental ones are dropped or loosened). ZOMBIES: Z full coverage lists no paths; O one unexercised path is named; M several are listed; B a path reached only by an error; I the measuring tool is named; E an unreviewed assertion blocks acceptance; S the report format is stable.
- **Flag decision:** ships behind a default-off flag (working agreement, line 82): an explicit opt-in switch on the CLI's synthesize path, later a project-profile key. Off leaves today's output unchanged.
- **Limits (stated plainly):** a characterization pins today's behaviour, bugs included; it does not certify it correct (suspected bugs are tagged as known quirks, so a later fix is a deliberate change, not drift). Only exercised behaviour is captured; unvisited paths stay unspecified. Capture needs a seam to observe each outcome. I/O, timing and concurrency may not be pinnable deterministically. Equivalence is judged only from externally observable outcomes, not internal call structure.
- **Out of scope:** legacy code in any source language other than C# until its adapter exists; generating other targets (card 296); fixing legacy defects; claiming complete coverage; migrating a production system.

## Context

- Value: teams with code they fear to change get a safety net first and a migration path second, and card 030's synthesis spike gets the behaviour oracle it needs. Ranked right after card 030.
- Persona: Morgan covers inherited C# code as well as Avowry source (PERSONAS.md, widened 2026-11-04 at this refinement). C# is the one supported adapter; other source languages come into scope as their adapters exist, each by its own card.
- Filed by the facilitator on 2026-11-04 from board refinement; split from one draft into this card and card 296 on the architect's and the domain expert's review.
